title: github-repos-audit snapshot
description: One complete reading of the account, as `github-repos-audit render` writes it to audit.json. The document carries collected facts, the declared repos.toml types and overrides; it carries no verdicts, which live only in the generated README table. Hand-maintained: the Go structs in internal/audit are the encoder, and this file is the contract they are held to. `additionalProperties` is false everywhere, so a new field is a deliberate edit here rather than an accident. Required means the Go tag has no `omitzero`, and therefore that the encoder always emits the key.

generated_at.description: When the run started, in UTC.

owner.description: The account every repository belongs to: the login of the token the run read with.

types.description: Every repository type repos.toml defines, keyed by type name: what each type expects of each check. Recorded so the document describes the standard each repository was judged against, not only its name. A type no repository uses is listed too. Never empty: config.Parse rejects a repos.toml with no [types.*] entries.

repos.description: Every declared repository the account has, sorted by name case-insensitively. Never empty: a run in which repos.toml names no repository the account has fails instead of writing a document.

identity.description: repos.toml's [identity] table: the identity git_identity holds the account holder's commits to. Absent when nothing judges git_identity, which is also the only case repos.toml may omit the table.

config_drift.description: Where repos.toml and the account disagree about which repositories exist. Absent when they agree.

claude_marketplace.description: The Claude plugin marketplace repos.toml's [claude] table names, read once per run. Absent when repos.toml configures none.

config_drift.description: The disagreement between repos.toml and the account. It stops nothing: the repositories both name are audited and appear in `repos`, and these are reported so the config gets fixed. At least one list is present.

unconfigured.description: Every repository the account has that repos.toml has no entry for, sorted by name case-insensitively. Named only: with no type to judge it against, it is not read and has no item in `repos`.

stale_entries.description: Every repos.toml entry naming a repository the account does not have: deleted, archived, or turned into a fork. Sorted by name case-insensitively.

repo.description: Everything known about one repository: what repos.toml declares and what GitHub answered.

name.description: The repository name on GitHub, which is the repos.toml table key.

type.description: The declared repos.toml type: a key of the top-level types object. JSON Schema cannot express that cross-reference; config.Parse enforces it.

published.description: The declared repos.toml flag: meant for a stranger to find and use.

overrides.description: The declared repos.toml override list, keyed by check name. Recorded so the document describes the standard each repository was actually held to. The values are free-form: config.validate rejects only an empty one, so an enum here would assert a contract the Go side does not keep.

propertyNames.description: Every check a repository can be judged on, in the fixed order the gap worklist reports them. internal/rules/schema_test.go asserts this enum equals rules.Checks(), in this order.

description.description: The repository description. Absent when unset.

homepage.description: The repository homepage URL. Absent when unset.

topics.description: How many topics the repository carries.

license.description: The SPDX identifier GitHub detected. NOASSERTION means it found a license file it could not identify, which is not a pass. Left unconstrained: the SPDX list grows, and internal/rules tests only for emptiness and NOASSERTION.

open_pull_requests.description: The count of open pull requests.

branches.description: How many branches the repository has, the default branch included. Zero for an empty repository. The report shows this count minus the default branch.

pushed_at.description: The last push to any branch, in UTC. Absent when the repository has never been pushed to.

default_branch.description: The live default branch name. Absent for an empty repository.

head_oid.description: The default branch's head commit, all forty characters. Abbreviating it silently breaks the smoke suite's cross-check, which answers total_count: 0 for a short SHA with a 200.

empty.description: A repository with no commits at all: GraphQL answered defaultBranchRef: null. Present only when true.

identities.description: Every distinct author and committer identity on the default branch's full history, exactly as the commits spell them, sorted by name then email. Includes other people and bots; which are the account holder's is internal/rules' decision. Absent for an empty repository.

workflow_facts.description: Every .yml or .yaml file in .github/workflows, parsed, sorted by path. Absent when there is none.

composite_actions.description: Every composite action in .github/actions, one per directory holding an action.yml or action.yaml, sorted by path. Absent when there is none.

ci_state.description: The statusCheckRollup state of the head commit. Absent when the rollup was null, which means no check has run on that commit.

rulesets.description: Every ruleset defined on the repository. Absent when there are none.

type.description: One type's expectations, keyed by check name. Every check is listed. The required list is in the order the gap worklist reports checks, which internal/rules/schema_test.go asserts equals rules.Checks(); the keys of an emitted document are alphabetical.

expectation.description: What a type asks of a check: required; not_required (never a gap); public (required only of a public repository); public_published (required only of a public, published one); info (shown, never judged).

direct_push.description: Whether a type expects pushing straight to the default branch to be blocked or allowed. Direct push is always judged.

info_expectation.description: A value-only check carries a value and never a pass or fail, so it is shown (info) or left out (not_required), never required.

release_age_threshold.description: What a type asks of the Renovate minimum release age: a duration such as "7 days" (expected, at least that long), not_required (never a gap) or info (shown, never judged). The pattern must match rules.ParseThreshold.

renovate.description: What the Renovate configuration says beyond where it lives. Absent when there is no configuration, or when nothing below was found.

min_release_age.description: The effective top-level minimumReleaseAge as written, after merging the repository's own file with the presets in the account it extends. Absent when unset, null or unresolved.

min_release_age_source.description: Where that value was set: the config path or the preset reference as written.

min_release_age_error.description: Why the configuration could not be decided: a missing or unparsable preset, a cycle, a template, a malformed minimumReleaseAge or stabilityDays. When set, nix_manager and lock_file_maintenance are absent too.

nix_manager.description: Whether Renovate's nix manager runs: nix.enabled true after the same merge, with enabledManagers unset or listing "nix". Absent when off, unset, of the wrong type or unresolved.

lock_file_maintenance.description: Whether lockFileMaintenance.enabled is true after the same merge, which for this key also reads the built-in presets the README lists under nix_lock_refresh. Absent when off, unset, of the wrong type or unresolved.

automerge_major.description: Whether Renovate merges every major update on its own after the same merge: automerge on for majors, with nothing disabling them, requiring Dependency Dashboard approval for them, or holding some of them in a narrower packageRule. Absent when off, unset, of the wrong type or unresolved.

files.description: The outcome of every file-existence probe. A probe answers null for a path that does not exist, so an absent file is an ordinary answer rather than an error.

readme.description: True when any of the six accepted README paths exists. Probes are case-sensitive, so a differently-cased file reads as missing.

gitignore.description: Matches `.gitignore` exactly. A looser match would report a typo'd `.gitigore` as a pass, which is the very thing this report exists to catch.

justfile.description: True when `justfile_path` is set. just matches the name case-insensitively.

security.description: Probed at all three locations GitHub recognises: the root, `.github/` and `docs/`.

renovate_config.description: Where the Renovate configuration lives: the first accepted path to match, in Renovate's own lookup order. Absent when there is none.

workflows.description: The entries of `.github/workflows`, sorted. Absent when the directory is empty or missing.

justfile_path.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The justfile, matched case-insensitively. Absent when no accepted name is present.

commitlint.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The commitlint configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

git_cliff.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The git-cliff configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

treefmt.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The treefmt configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

typos.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The typos configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

yamllint.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The yamllint configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

markdownlint.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The markdownlint configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

prettier.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The Prettier configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

editorconfig_checker.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The editorconfig-checker configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

lychee.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The lychee configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

zizmor.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The zizmor configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

codecov.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The Codecov configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

mkdocs.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The MkDocs configuration. Absent when no accepted name is present.

license_file.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The license text, or the `LICENSES/` directory (trailing slash). Absent when no accepted name is present.

security_policy.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The security policy, matched case-insensitively. Absent when no accepted name is present.

codeowners.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The CODEOWNERS file. Absent when no accepted name is present.

pr_template.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The pull request template file or directory (trailing slash). Absent when no accepted name is present.

claude_md.description: Where the file was found in the tree at HEAD, as the tree spells it. The Claude Code memory file. Absent when no accepted name is present.

compose.description: The distinct compose file names found at any depth, sorted. Absent when there are none.

go_mod.description: A file named exactly go.mod at the root. Absent when there is none.

flake.description: What flake.lock says. Absent when there is no flake.lock; files.flake_nix, not this object, says whether flake.nix exists.

nixpkgs_last_modified.description: locked.lastModified of the node the root's nixpkgs input resolves to, in UTC. Absent when there is no lock or no input named nixpkgs.

all_rev_pinned.description: Every non-root node's `original` carries `rev`. Absent when false, which includes a lock with no inputs.

lock_error.description: Why flake.lock could not be read. When present none of the other lock facts is.

workflow.description: What one GitHub Actions workflow file says, values kept as written.

path.description: The file's path in the repository, such as ".github/workflows/ci.yml".

parse_error.description: Why the file could not be read as a workflow: invalid YAML, a shape GitHub would not run, or a blob that is binary or too large to read in full. When present nothing but path is.

events.description: The trigger names under `on:`, sorted and without repeats.

pull_request_types.description: The `types:` listed for `pull_request` under the map form of `on:`, sorted and without repeats. Absent when the trigger lists none: with `pull_request` in `events` that is GitHub's default set, `opened`, `synchronize` and `reopened`.

pull_request_target_types.description: The `types:` listed for `pull_request_target` under the map form of `on:`, sorted and without repeats. Absent when the trigger lists none: with `pull_request_target` in `events` that is GitHub's default set, `opened`, `synchronize` and `reopened`.

pull_request_branches.description: The `branches:` listed for `pull_request` under the map form of `on:`, in written order with repeats kept. GitHub matches them against the pull request's base branch. Absent when the trigger lists none.

pull_request_branches_ignore.description: The `branches-ignore:` listed for `pull_request` under the map form of `on:`, in written order with repeats kept. Absent when the trigger lists none; never present beside `pull_request_branches`.

pull_request_target_branches.description: The `branches:` listed for `pull_request_target` under the map form of `on:`, in written order with repeats kept. GitHub matches them against the pull request's base branch. Absent when the trigger lists none.

pull_request_target_branches_ignore.description: The `branches-ignore:` listed for `pull_request_target` under the map form of `on:`, in written order with repeats kept. Absent when the trigger lists none; never present beside `pull_request_target_branches`.

push_branches.description: The `branches:` listed for `push` under the map form of `on:`, in written order with repeats kept, because a `!` pattern only excludes what the patterns before it matched. Absent when the trigger lists none.

push_branches_ignore.description: The `branches-ignore:` listed for `push` under the map form of `on:`, in written order with repeats kept. Absent when the trigger lists none; never present beside `push_branches`.

push_tag_filter.description: `push` lists `tags:` or `tags-ignore:`. With no branch filter beside it, branch pushes never trigger the workflow. Absent when false.

reusable.description: The job calls a reusable workflow with a job-level `uses:`.

timeout_minutes.description: `timeout-minutes:` as written, an expression included. Absent when the key is.

concurrency.description: A `concurrency:` setting, at workflow or job level.

set.description: `concurrency:` is present in either form; an explicit null is not presence.

cancel_in_progress.description: `cancel-in-progress:` exactly as written: "true", "false" or an expression. Absent when the key is, and always for the string form.

permissions.description: A `permissions:` setting, at workflow or job level.

set.description: `permissions:` is present in either form; an explicit null is not presence.

scopes.description: The map form, scope name to access as written. Empty for `permissions: {}`, which grants nothing.

step_use.description: One step that runs an action.

with.description: The step's `with:` inputs, every value a scalar kept as written. Absent when there are none.

composite_action.description: What one composite action's action.yml or action.yaml says.

path.description: The file's path in the repository, such as ".github/actions/setup/action.yml".

parse_error.description: As a workflow's parse_error: when present nothing but path is.

uses.description: Every step's `uses:` under runs.steps, in step order. Absent for a JavaScript or Docker action.

claude.description: What the repository's Claude Code skills, command files, hooks and plugin manifest say. Absent when it has none of them. When unreadable is present nothing but plugin is.

skills.description: Every SKILL.md Claude Code would load, sorted by path.

commands.description: Every command file, sorted by path, then every inline command plugin.json declares, sorted by name.

hooks.description: Every hook handler, from hook files, an inline plugin.json hooks object and skill or command frontmatter, sorted by source then event.

unreadable.description: A problem with the Claude files as a whole: "too many Claude files", a plugin manifest whose layout cannot be decided, or "plugin.json declares missing <path>".

claude_skill.description: One skill or command file. A command file is recorded in a skill's shape.

path.description: The file's path, or .claude-plugin/plugin.json#commands/<name> for an inline command.

dir.description: The name Claude Code knows it by: the skill's directory, the plugin's name for a root SKILL.md, or the command's name. Empty for the root SKILL.md of a plugin whose manifest sets no name.

keys.description: Every frontmatter key, mapped to the YAML tag of its value, such as "!!str" or "!!bool".

has_description.description: `description` is a YAML string holding more than whitespace.

description_chars.description: The combined length in characters of `description` and `when_to_use`.

wraps_skill.description: For a command, the one skill its body names. Absent for a skill, and for a command naming no skill or several.

unreadable.description: Why the file could not be read in full or parsed. When present nothing but path and dir is.

claude_hook.description: One handler of one hook event.

source.description: The file the hook is declared in.

plugin.description: A plugin declares the hook: in a plugin hooks file, the manifest, or a plugin skill's frontmatter.

event.description: The hook event name as written.

type.description: The handler type as written, such as command, http, mcp_tool, prompt or agent.

matcher.description: The group's matcher. Absent when unset or empty.

timeout.description: The handler's timeout in seconds. Absent when unset or zero; timeout_set tells the two apart.

script.description: The repository file a command handler runs. Absent when it names none.

interpreter.description: The script is handed to an interpreter, which reads it rather than executing it.

path_form.description: How the command names its program. Absent for a bare command on PATH.

script_mode.description: The git mode of the tracked file at script, such as "100755". Absent when script is not a tracked file.

unreadable.description: Why the hooks could not be read. When present nothing but source and plugin is.

claude_marketplace.description: What the configured marketplace repository's .claude-plugin/marketplace.json lists, with what GitHub answered about each entry's pin.

repo.description: The marketplace repository's name, as repos.toml's [claude] table gives it.

unreadable.description: Why the marketplace could not be read: the account does not have the repository, or its marketplace.json is absent or not in the shape Claude Code loads. When present entries is absent.

entries.description: Every plugins entry, in the file's order.

marketplace_entry.description: One marketplace plugins entry and the answers about its pin. The lookups are made only for an entry whose source is a GitHub repository of the audited account.

name.description: The entry's name, the plugin's install id.

repo.description: The source's owner/name as written. Absent for a source that is not a GitHub repository.

ref.description: The source's ref as written. Absent when unset.

sha.description: The source's sha as written. Absent when unset.

has_version.description: The entry carries a version key, which plugin.json should own instead.

release_tag.description: ref names a release of repo.

tag_commit.description: The commit the tag ref resolves to, annotated tags dereferenced. Absent when repo has no such tag.

problem.description: Why a lookup could not be made or gave no usable answer: the source is not an audited repository, the tag resolves to no commit, or there is no readable manifest at sha.

claude_plugin.description: What .claude-plugin/plugin.json says. Absent when there is none.

fields.description: Every required manifest field present, sorted.

unreadable.description: Why the manifest could not be read in full or parsed. When present name, version and fields are absent.

ci.description: The timing of the repository's recent CI, recorded per commit. No means and no selection: which commits a figure is taken over, and what an incomplete or bot-authored commit contributes, is decided when the report is rendered. Absent when the repository has no merged pull requests and no commits.

pull_requests.description: The head commit of each recently merged pull request, in the order GitHub listed them: most recently updated first, which is not merge order.

default_branch.description: The most recent default-branch commits, newest first, whether or not any workflow ran on them.

last_default_branch_run.description: When the newest workflow run on the default branch from this repository, not a fork's pull request from a branch of the same name, was created, of any event, in UTC. Absent when no such run is among the newest hundred runs on that branch name, and for an empty repository.

ci_commit.description: One commit's GitHub Actions workflow runs, reduced to timestamp arithmetic. A check another app posts is not counted.

pr_number.description: The pull request this commit was the head of. Absent for a default-branch entry.

merged_at.description: When that pull request merged, in UTC. Absent for a default-branch entry.

author_bot.description: The pull request's author is a GitHub App's bot account. Present only when true.

complete.description: At least one workflow run, every run and every job completed with a known completion time, no jobs list cut short by its page size, and at least one job finished.

wait_seconds.description: The latest job completion over the commit's runs minus the earliest run creation, in seconds. Present only when complete and positive.

jobs.description: Every job that completed with both timestamps, in the order GitHub listed them. Absent when there is none.

seconds.description: The job's completion minus its start: time on a runner, not time queued for one.

actions_storage.description: What the repository holds in GitHub Actions storage, sizes in bytes as GitHub reports them. Absent for an empty repository, which is not read for it, or when all four answers are zero.

caches.description: Every cache entry, sorted by key, then ref, then creation time. last_accessed_at is not recorded: it changes on every restore. Absent when there is none.

cache_usage_bytes.description: The total size of the active caches, GitHub's own usage figure.

cache_limit_bytes.description: The repository's cache storage limit: max_cache_size_gb × 1,000,000,000. Absent when no limit was read.

artifact_count.description: How many artifacts have not expired.

artifact_bytes.description: The total size of the artifacts that have not expired.

key.description: The cache key as the saving step wrote it.

ref.description: The ref the cache was saved from, refs/heads/<branch> or refs/pull/<number>/merge.

created_at.description: When the entry was saved, in UTC.

releases.description: A summary of the repository's releases.

drafts.description: How many of the five most recent releases are drafts. The published count is total minus drafts.

last_published_at.description: When the most recent non-draft release was published, in UTC. Absent when there is none.

latest_tag.description: The tag of GitHub's Latest release, which excludes drafts and prereleases. Absent when there is none.

latest_published_at.description: When GitHub's Latest release was published, in UTC. Absent when there is none.

identity.description: One git identity as a commit spells it. Either half may be empty: GitHub answers null for a name or address the commit does not carry, and the other half is still a fact.

identity_standard.description: The account holder's git identity standard. canonical is the one correct identity, written "Name <email>"; match is an unanchored RE2 expression tested against each commit identity's "Name <email>", and whatever it matches is the account holder's. Identities listed in accepted are the account holder's but never wrong.

accepted.description: Further identities, each written "Name <email>", that are the account holder's and acceptable though not canonical — the account's GitHub noreply identity, which GitHub records on merges and edits made in its web UI, typically. Absent when none are declared.

ruleset.description: One repository ruleset, with the conditions and rules needed to tell a tag ruleset from a branch one and an active ruleset from an evaluated one.

include.description: conditions.refName.include, such as ["refs/tags/**"] or ["~DEFAULT_BRANCH"]. Absent when empty.

rules.description: Every rule type the ruleset carries, such as PULL_REQUEST. Left unconstrained: GitHub adds rule types, and internal/rules matches the handful it names rather than switching over the set.

branch_rules.description: The rule set as evaluated for the default branch, which is precisely the "can I push straight to it?" question.

known.description: False for an empty repository, whose default branch does not exist, so the endpoint is never called.

types.description: Every rule type in force on the branch, lowercase as REST spells them. Absent when there are none.

required_checks.description: The context name of each required status check. Absent when there are none.

strict.description: True when any required_status_checks rule in force asks for the branch to be up to date before merging. GitHub applies it only with at least one required check. Absent when false.

settings.description: Every live repository setting. Most feed the modal computation: nothing has a declared expected value, so the tool computes the most common value across the repositories where the setting applies and reports the ones that differ. secret_scanning and private_vulnerability_reporting are judged as the secret_scanning and vuln_reporting checks instead.

merge_commit_title.description: GraphQL's MergeCommitTitle enum. Absent when GitHub omitted it.

merge_commit_message.description: GraphQL's MergeCommitMessage enum. Absent when GitHub omitted it.

secret_scanning.description: Absent when GitHub omitted the security_and_analysis block entirely, which it does for a private repository on a personal plan. Absent means n/a, not disabled.

secret_scanning_push_protection.description: Follows the same convention as secret_scanning.

private_vulnerability_reporting.description: Absent when the endpoint answered 404, which it does for a private repository. Absent means n/a, not disabled.

allowed_actions.description: Present only under the "selected" policy: the selected-actions endpoint answers 404 under any other policy, and 409 under "all".

can_approve_pull_requests.description: Whether the workflow token may approve pull requests.

actions_access_level.description: Whether this repository's actions are reusable from other repositories. Absent for a public repository, where the endpoint answers 422 — the setting does not exist there.

patterns.description: The allowlist itself, sorted. Absent when empty.
